Readout: the related hesitation seen in session 3. The wireflow says step 4 can be skipped (audit follow-up §3).

entries.evidence: user-flows/onboarding-flow: "Step 3 — Connect calendar (now clearly marked required)"; step 4 isn't marked required. finding:onboarding and the readout: step 3 is required though its wording reads as optional. Raw sessions 1–2: participants tried to skip the calendar step and hit the "required" indicator; session 2 calls it "step 2" (the audit's two numbering conventions). Wireflow: "Only step 3 is required … so step 4 can be skipped." No record says Basics or Signup can be skipped. The patterns key on step names, not numbers, because the calendar step is "step 2" in the raw notes and step 3 in the canonical flow. Baseline answer states "Step 2 (Basics) can be skipped" with no citation.

entries.question: What did nurses want from the citations in the prior auth drafts?

mustClaims.description: Inline citations to the specific chart entries or text behind each claim ("show your work")

mustNotClaims.description: Overstates the count: 3 of 4 asked unprompted in v1, and 3 of 4 clicked a citation in v2

entries.evidence: Raw v1 (2025-04-08): participants wanted to see which specific chart entries the AI pulled from, inline; "show your work" was mentioned unprompted by 3 of 4; P17: "Show me where it got that info." Recommendation: inline source citations (chart entry + date) for every claim. Raw v2: 3 of 4 clicked into at least one citation. finding:prior-authorization, the drafting panel component and the v2 service topology restate the requirement.

mustNotClaims.description: Overstates recognition: 5 of 6 recognized the flag

entries.evidence: Raw 2026-01-13 (GA candidate): sound-alike errors still in 1 of 6 sessions; treat as post-GA monitoring, not a blocker. Raw 2026-02-10 (concept test): a distinct amber pill badge; 5 of 6 recognized it as different from the generic underline; 2 of 6 said it made them trust unflagged lines more; inline placement preferred 5:1. finding:ambient-scribe-post-ga-refinements and finding:ambient-scribe summarize both; the wireframe and thumbnails show the placement.

entries.question: What are clinicians' biggest pain points with documentation?

mustClaims.description: After-hours charting: physicians finishing documentation after clinic hours ("pajama time")
mustClaims.pattern: after[- ](clinic[- ])?hours|after (clinic|work|the clinic day)|pajama|at night|in the evening|\bat home\b|after (the )?kids

mustClaims.description: A documentation pain point beyond the burnout ranking: re-entering the same fields, or the underlying EHR problems (cross-referencing systems and chart-review time are care coordinators' pain, not documentation pain, and don't count)

mustNotClaims.description: Turns 52% (documentation as physicians' #1 burnout contributor) into a burnout rate
Attributes the 52% to clinicians, nurses or all respondents; the survey figure is physicians'

entries.evidence: Raw survey 2025-09-09 (research/raw/2025-09-09-survey-clinician-burnout-documentation-burden-baseline/session-notes.md, survey, attitudinal): "Documentation burden ranked as the #1 self-selected contributor to burnout among physicians specifically (52%)"; "64% of physician respondents report regularly completing documentation after clinic hours ('pajama time'), averaging a self-reported 1.2 hours/day"; P84: "I do not love finishing my notes at 9pm"; P91: "don't let 'AI will fix documentation' become the excuse to skip fixing the actual EHR problems". Its own caveat: respondents were told the survey related to an AI initiative. Raw contextual inquiry 2025-04-22 (research/raw/2025-04-22-contextual-inquiry-ed-intake-shadowing/session-notes.md, behavioral): P23 "stop making me type the same sixteen fields". Raw nursing survey 2025-02-11: P41 "if it got me out of the room 10 minutes faster to chart" (its top concern, narrative voice, is about AI, not documentation pain). finding:clinician-experience-documentation-burden repeats the burnout survey. The burnout survey is required because it is the only raw record about documentation burden across clinicians. Coverage report (2026-09-29): the pipeline cited it but only repeated the burnout statistics, and the ED intake inquiry didn't reach the model. The chart-review inquiry (2025-01-29) is not a supporting record: its "cross-reference 3-4 systems" and "8-14 minutes per patient" chart review are care coordinators' pain before outreach calls, not documentation pain.

entries.question: Why didn't physicians trust the ambient scribe's draft notes?

mustClaims.description: Medication (dosage or drug-name) errors in the drafts
Accuracy improvements alone didn't change trust: physicians still read every line after the errors dropped
mustClaims.pattern: (accura|fix|improv|fewer errors|errors (dropped|fell|decreased))[^.]{0,150}(alone|by itself|on (its|their) own|didn't|did not|not enough|wasn't enough|still)[^.]{0,100}(trust|read(ing)? every|skim)|still read(s|ing)? every (line|word)|(trust|reading behavio)\w*[^.]{0,40}(didn't|did not|doesn't|does not) (shift|change|move|improve)

mustNotClaims.description: Says the accuracy fixes resolved or restored trust; v0.2 found trust unchanged despite them (the window crosses version dots such as "v0.2")

entries.evidence: Raw v0.2 2025-09-23 (research/raw/2025-09-23-usability-test-ambient-scribe-v02/session-notes.md, usability test, behavioral): "Despite accuracy improvements, all 5 participants still read every line before accepting … suggesting trust doesn't shift from accuracy improvements alone"; P09: "Getting it right once doesn't mean I trust it yet." Required because it holds the why. Raw v0.1 2025-02-25 (research/raw/2025-02-25-usability-test-ambient-scribe-v01/session-notes.md, behavioral): "missed or garbled medication dosages in 3 of 5 — physicians said this was disqualifying for direct sign-off"; "4 of 5 participants read every line"; P09: "I have to read every word anyway right now … Ask me again in a month." Raw GA candidate 2026-01-13: "4 of 6 participants said it let them skim high-confidence lines for the first time" (confidence highlighting, not accuracy, moved trust). finding:ambient-scribe: "Trust calibration was the hardest problem, and accuracy alone didn't solve it." The persona and journey map restate it. Method caveat (coverage report): the behavior is well observed, but the why rests on in-session quotes; there is no physician interview. Coverage report: the pipeline cited v0.1 only; v0.2 ranked #8 and wasn't shown, so the answer missed that accuracy alone didn't change trust.

entries.evidence: Raw prior-auth v1 2025-04-08 (research/raw/2025-04-08-usability-test-prior-auth-ai-v1/session-notes.md, usability test, behavioral with unprompted requests): "Participants wanted to see which specific chart entries the AI pulled from, inline, rather than trusting a black-box summary — 'show your work' was mentioned unprompted by 3 of 4"; Utilization Review Nurse, P17: "Five minutes saved is great until it's the case that gets denied and now I'm on the phone with the payer for 40 minutes instead. Show me where it got that info." (the reason: a denied case costs about 40 minutes on the phone with the payer). Recommendation: "Add inline source citations (chart entry + date) for every claim". entries.question: How did new admins expect the invite step to work?

mustClaims.description: When invites are sent: admins worried or weren't sure whether invites go out immediately (emailing the whole team before they're ready) or only when setup is finished

mustNotClaims.description: Says step 4 / Invite your team is required or can't be skipped; the wireflow says it can be skipped
mustNotClaims.pattern: (invite your team|invite step|invitation step|step 4)[\"”')]*[^.,;]{0,25}((?<!not |n't )\b(is|are|was) (also )?(required|mandatory)|can(no|'|’)t be skipped)

mustNotClaims.description: Generalizes the worry to all or most participants; the raw notes record it for one session (session 3)

entries.evidence: Raw onboarding test 2026-01-19 (research/raw/2026-01-19-onboarding-usability-test/session-notes.md, usability test; the answer to a direct probe is attitudinal): Session 3: "When asked directly, said: 'I guess I'm worried this is going to email my whole team before I'm ready.'" The raw note places it at "step 3" and never uses the word "invite"; finding:onboarding moves it to step 4 ("Invite your team") by reconciling the two numbering schemes and says admins "aren't sure whether invites send immediately or only when the wizard is" submitted. Topline: "All 3 participants paused at step 4" (the raw notes don't support "all 3"). Journey map: "worried invites are sending before" she's ready. Readout: recommends visible feedback that invites aren't sent until submit. The storyboard is a made-up scenario and isn't a supporting record. Method caveat: a mental-model question answered by one probe answer; the guide's "what do you expect to happen next" answers weren't written down. Coverage report: the raw session ranked #14 (its roster outscored its notes) and the answer cited the topline and the storyboard.

entries.question: What evidence supports making the calendar step required in onboarding?

mustClaims.description: Premise check: says the calendar step is already required
Premise check: says no record argues for (or gives a reason for) making it required
mustClaims.pattern: \b(no|none of the|not any|nothing|neither)\b[^.]{0,80}\b(argu|support|evidence|justif|rationale|reason|case)\w*[^.]{0,80}(requir|mandator)|\b(do not|don't|does not|doesn't|did not|didn't)\b[^.]{0,40}\b(argue|make (a|the) case|justify|give (a )?(reason|rationale)|support|explain why)\w*[^.]{0,80}(requir|mandator)

mustNotClaims.description: Presents the skip attempts, hesitation or drop-off as evidence for requiring the step

entries.evidence: Premise check. The step is already required: deliverable:user-flows/onboarding-flow: "Step 3 — Connect calendar (now clearly marked required)"; finding:onboarding: its wording implies it is optional "when it's actually required for later functionality" (no source is given for that rationale). No record, raw or synthesis, argues for requiring it; the evidence supports labeling it clearly, and if anything shows the requirement causes friction. Raw onboarding test 2026-01-19 (research/raw/2026-01-19-onboarding-usability-test/session-notes.md, usability test, behavioral): session 1 "paused ~15s at step 3 ('Connect calendar'), said 'wait, do I have to do this?'"; session 2 "Backed out when the 'required' indicator appeared … ('could've told me that up front')"; sessions 4–6: "none independently identified it as required without hitting the 'required' state first". analytics:onboarding-funnel-dropoff: step 3 is the largest drop-off, read as users "not realizing the step is required" (the raw export isn't in the corpus). Readout and topline: relabel step 3. Deciding whether it should be required would need attitudinal evidence, which the corpus doesn't have. Coverage report: the pipeline accepted the premise and listed the skip attempts as evidence for requiring it. Expected to fail on today's answers.

entries.evidence: Open questions, no acceptDecline: a decline citing nothing fails. Raw contextual inquiry 2025-01-29 (research/raw/2025-01-29-contextual-inquiry-chart-review-baseline/session-notes.md, discovery, behavioral), Follow-ups / Open Questions: "Quantify how often the AVS tool has missed medication changes — pull incident/complaint logs if they exist." and "Revisit with float-pool coordinators specifically; they may have different pain points due to less system familiarity." What it shows: coordinators "manually cross-reference 3-4 systems"; they "distrust auto-generated summaries from the EHR's built-in 'AVS'"; P05 (float pool): "If it could just tell me what changed since I last touched this chart". Raw usability test 2025-08-26 (research/raw/2025-08-26-usability-test-alert-triage-ai-care-coordination/session-notes.md, behavioral): "4 of 5 participants disagreed with the AI's top-3 ranking … the model weighted 'recency' more heavily than coordinators' own sense of clinical risk"; no way to note why they reprioritized; recommendation to "Investigate incorporating patient history/continuity signals into ranking logic … before wider testing". Gaps not written as follow-ups (credit, not required): the override-reason wireflow was never tested; "what changed since last review" was never built or tested; triage speed was measured only in simulation; there is no coordinator interview, and the mental model is inferred from overrides. Coverage report: the pipeline declined ("The sources do not say…"), citing nothing; both raw sessions were shown only as their participant rosters. Expected to fail on today's answers.
